review.summary:
Correctness and concurrency review of the walking skeleton. I read crates/store (commit, read, tail, layouts, presence, migrations), the app handlers (scan, map, focus, person, actor, share, import, data, workspace), live.rs, server/ (mod, routes, auth), kernel keys/tree/facts, and extract files/walk/verify/lines, and I checked them against contracts.md, architecture.md and the DRs. I ran target/debug/planroom on fresh copies of the fixture from examples/build-fixture in the scratchpad, with PLANROOM_DATA pointed at temporary directories.

Verified by running the binary:
- (1) The first scan of a commit stores whatever the working tree held, and later scans of that commit never correct it. A clean rescan still lacked 5 containers and a committed CHANGELOG.md.
- (2) Untracked directories and empty untracked files enter the map.
- (3) A repo that leaves the workspace stays on the map. The scan said "Mapped 4 repos" while the map showed 5.
- (4) workspaces.json loses unknown fields, min_reader_version among them.
- (5) Two concurrent `serve --detach` in one workspace both succeed on different ports.

Also verified, and working: concurrent first scans join on one set of events (3 parallel scans x 6 runs, 5 events each). A head moving A->B->A->B->A->B records each move.

Found by reading code only, not run: the other findings. They are (6) torn reads, (7) the canvas subscribe gap, (8) a second envelope from serve, (9) a stale packs_hash, (10) live/head's seq bookkeeping, (11) a live loop that dies silently and (12) a store file left unmigrated.

Left out because the docs already schedule them: the SSE broadcast-lag reset, `serve` reuse and drain, the commit-time store-version check, and meta.dirty_repos.

Not tested: whether ArtifactData `update` deep-merges `acks/<uid>.rows`. I couldn't run it.

The plugin guard blocked direct reads of store.db and serve.json, so I used `watch --json` to inspect the event log.

findings.title: A snapshot is keyed by the HEAD commit but built from the working tree, so the first scan of a commit freezes a dirty tree's facts and later clean rescans never correct them
findings.evidence:
Verified by running the binary. scan.rs:108 walks the working tree. The facts are stored under the snapshot (repo, HEAD commit, packs_hash). put_snapshot is INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (commit.rs:303), and insert_facts runs only when `created` (commit.rs:156). previous == snapshot then reports Unchanged (commit.rs:160).

Repro 1, on a fresh fixture copy: prepend '# local note' to platform/docker-compose.yml (uncommitted) and run `scan`. It warns evidence_dropped, 27 items. The map shows only the 5 repos, and the 5 ws:container:* nodes are gone. Restore the file (`git status` clean) and `scan` again. Still 5 repos, 0 containers, and 'Mapped ... 0 of them moved'.

Repro 2: move kit/CHANGELOG.md away, scan, move it back (clean tree), scan. `map --level code` reports kit:file:CHANGELOG.md MISSING, while the scan line claims 135 nodes. The map now depends on the working tree at the first scan of each commit, not on the commit.
findings.why: The map is wrong and stays wrong, with no recovery until HEAD moves. Two stores at the same heads give different maps, which is not deterministic. It contradicts architecture.md:609 ('The map holds only committed lines'). A person's first scan of a real repo is often dirty, so S1/S2-style answers on a real workspace silently lose components. Any rescan-based reconcile (S4 step 4/5) reads a frozen snapshot.
findings.fix: Extract from the commit's blobs (git ls-tree plus cat-file through the existing Objects adapter) rather than the working tree, so the facts are a pure function of the snapshot key. If the working-tree walk must stay, make the snapshot key include a hash of the verified fact set, so a different fact set creates a new snapshot instead of reusing the old one.

findings.title: Ref evidence verifies paths that aren't in the commit: untracked directories and empty untracked files reach the map
findings.evidence: Verified by running the binary. On a fresh copy, `mkdir -p kit/scratch/deep && echo notes > kit/scratch/deep/notes.txt && touch kit/EMPTY_UNTRACKED` (git status shows both as ??), then `scan`. The file inside is dropped (1 evidence_dropped). But `map --level component` lists kit:dir:scratch and kit:dir:scratch/deep, and `map --level code` lists kit:file:EMPTY_UNTRACKED. Directories, empty files and non-UTF-8 files carry Evidence::Ref {commit, branch}. Verifier::check only checks that the commit and ref exist, never that the path is in that commit's tree. Combined with correctness-1, these nodes then persist after the files are removed.
findings.why: The evidence claims a commit holds something it doesn't. That breaks the stated rule that the map holds only committed content (architecture.md:609, DR-71/DR-81) and the evidence-at-ingest guarantee (DR-12).
findings.fix: Give directory and empty-file nodes evidence that names the path (for example a Ref plus path, checked with `git cat-file -e <commit>:<path>`), and drop a directory node when none of its files survive verification.

findings.title: A repo that leaves the workspace (deleted, moved or renamed) stays on the map forever
findings.evidence: Verified by running the binary. In a scanned fixture copy, `mv kit elsewhere`, then `scan . --json`. The text summary says 'Mapped 4 repos, 0 of them moved', but result.map.nodes still contains kit:repo:kit. active_snapshots takes the last scan event per target, and nothing ever retires a target. commit_scan only adds or moves repos in `active` and builds the link from all of them. The event model has no 'repo removed' body. A directory rename (which DR-74 says namespaces survive) shows both the old and the new repo.
findings.why: This is a design gap the skeleton revealed: the 'living map' shows a system that no longer exists, with no command to correct it. The only recovery is deleting the store, which in M1+ loses person-authored events (KICKOFF principle 1, 'never lose what someone did'). The scan's own reply (4 repos) and its map (5) disagree.
findings.fix: In commit_scan, for each active repo absent from ScanWrite.repos, append a scan-family event (for example `repo_removed`, an additive EventBody) that drops it from the active set and rebuilds the link snapshot. Have active_snapshots honour it. Treat a rename through DR-74's meta.repos mapping.

findings.title: workspaces.json is rewritten without a lock and drops every field this build doesn't know, min_reader_version included
findings.evidence: Verified by running the binary. I wrote a workspaces.json with top-level "min_reader_version":"0.1.0" and "future_key":1, and an entry with "label". Then `serve --detach --port 41777`. The rewritten file holds only format and workspaces[{root, workspace_id, port}]; all three unknown fields were gone. `record` deserializes into a struct with no #[serde(flatten)] extra, then does a read-modify-write rename with no file lock. Two engines recording at once (two workspaces' first serve) lose one entry.
findings.why: This violates the AGENTS.md compatibility invariant ('Readers of persisted documents ... keep fields they don't know') and contracts.md:14. contracts.md:357 says this file is shared by every engine version on the machine and changes only by additions. An older engine erasing min_reader_version defeats DR-78's guard. A lost entry lets a workspace's port move, which DR-78 forbids, and that strands a tab's sessionStorage token and pending edits.
findings.fix: Add `#[serde(flatten)] extra: Map<String, Value>` to Workspaces and WorkspaceEntry, and write them back. Hold an flock on workspaces.json.lock across read, modify and rename. Check min_reader_version on read.

findings.title: Two concurrent first `serve --detach` runs in one workspace both start, on different ports; one is orphaned
findings.evidence: Verified by running the binary. Fresh data root, two `serve --detach --json` at once in one workspace. Both returned ok, port 43473 pid 7197 and port 45747 pid 7198. workspaces.json recorded only 45747, and both processes stayed up until I killed them. With no recorded port, `bind` binds port 0 in each process, and the last `record` wins. serve.json is likewise last-writer-wins, so it can name the other port.
findings.why: This is a design gap that the planned reuse through serve.json (architecture.md:156, 1271, 1603) won't close, because that is also check-then-act. Two surfaces (the pane's `e` and `/room open`) racing on first use leave an unreachable server and can record a port that serve.json disagrees with.
findings.fix: Take an exclusive lock (for example flock on .planroom/serve.lock) across reading serve.json and workspaces.json, binding and recording, and release it after serve.json is written. The second caller then sees the first and reuses it.

findings.title: Reads aren't in one read transaction, so a reply's meta.seq can be newer than its content and the active set can be torn
findings.evidence: Found by reading code only. map::run folds through active_set (two separate SELECTs: per-repo scans, then the last scan's link) and facts, then reads store.seq() afterwards (map.rs:40). Each statement is its own autocommit read, so a commit between them returns content from N-1 with meta.seq = N, or repos from one scan and the link from another. contracts.md:94 defines seq as 'the highest seq inside the one read', and architecture.md:384 (DR-73) says a read takes N inside that transaction so that 'a writer's base never covers a write it didn't see'.
findings.why: Writes aren't built yet, so the harm is latent. But meta.seq is already returned and documented as the base a writer uses (architecture.md:434-435), and the M1 base check will trust it.
findings.fix: Add a Store read-snapshot method that opens one `BEGIN` (deferred) transaction and reads active set, facts and max seq inside it, and route map, focus, share and import through it.

findings.title: The canvas subscribes to the stream after loading, with no `since`, so a commit in between never triggers a refetch
findings.evidence: Found by reading code only. start() awaits load() (map and focus), then calls transport.subscribe(). The first stream request carries no Last-Event-ID (lastId starts null) and no since, and the server starts the cursor at the store's latest seq (backlog: Live::new(tail, None) leaves the cursor at latest). A commit landing after the map read and before the stream request sends no frame, so the canvas shows the old map until some later commit.
findings.why: S8 (tier A) requires live updates within 1 s while several writers commit. A final write that lands in this window is never shown, which makes S8 flaky.
findings.fix: Have subscribe take the loaded view's meta.seq and send `?since=SEQ` on the first connection. The server already replays the backlog for `since`.

findings.title: A foreground `serve --json` prints a second JSON document when serving fails after its success envelope
findings.evidence: Found by reading code only. In the non-detached path, announce() is printed through cli::finish (one envelope). Then `serve(prepared)` runs, and on Err calls cli::finish::<()>(json, "serve", Err(e), started) again, a second document on stdout. Possible errors include the Tokio runtime build, Store::open_existing in serve() (for example the store migrated or removed between prepare and serve), and axum::serve failing.
findings.why: AGENTS.md: '`--json` mode prints exactly one JSON document on stdout'. A client parsing the stream reads two envelopes, and may read the first ok:true and miss the failure.
findings.fix: After the success envelope has gone out, report a later failure on stderr (and through the exit code) only, as the detached child already does.

findings.title: meta.packs_hash is written only once, so after an engine upgrade it disagrees with the hash new snapshots carry
findings.evidence: Found by reading code only. packs_hash() includes the engine's CARGO_PKG_VERSION (DR-62), so it changes with every release. scan stores it with meta_insert_once, which never overwrites. After an upgrade, every new snapshot uses the new hash while meta keeps the first engine's.
findings.why: architecture.md:243 has every read compare 'the recorded packs_hash' with the active snapshot to decide on a rescan. Built on this value, freshness would rescan on every read forever, or never detect a pack change. Nothing reads it yet.
findings.fix: Write packs and packs_hash inside commit_scan's transaction (an upsert), together with the snapshots that use them.

findings.title: live/head's seq bookkeeping can skip changes the published page never saw, and can list changes past head.seq
findings.evidence: Found by reading code only. (a) `share` sets meta.share_snapshot_seq when it writes the bundle to disk, before (and whether or not) the session publishes it. A second `share --out` that isn't published, or a failed publish, moves it forward. import's live_head then starts at that seq, so the page built from the earlier snapshot never gets the events in between. (b) import reads seq (import.rs:173), then pages events_after in a loop with no upper bound, so a commit in between appears in head.changes with seq > head.seq. The page uses head.seq as the base of its writes.
findings.why: The remote page can show a map missing changes with no sign of it, and its later writes carry a base older than what it displayed. That becomes spurious conflicts once M1/M5 apply rows.
findings.fix: Record the snapshot seq only after the publish succeeds (have the mod confirm it, for example with `share --published SEQ`), or store it in the published snapshot and have import read it from the inbox or head. Bound the live_head events by `seq` and read both in one read transaction.

findings.title: serve's live loop thread dies silently on any error other than schema_mismatch, and the server keeps running with no live frames
findings.evidence: Found by reading code only. start_live spawns a thread that runs live.run once. On Err other than SchemaMismatch it prints to stderr and returns. A transient store_busy (data_version, count_after and events_after all run under the 5 s busy timeout) or any Sqlite error is enough. Every SSE client stays connected and receives nothing more, not even pings: the per-client stream yields only broadcast frames, and the pings come from that loop.
findings.why: Canvases stop updating with no error shown. S8 requires live updates within 1 s.
findings.fix: Retry transient errors (Busy) in the loop with backoff, and on a fatal one send a Reset frame and exit the process (as for schema_mismatch), so the resolver or mod restarts serve.

findings.title: A store file left unmigrated makes every read command fail with internal until the next scan
findings.evidence: Found by reading code only. I couldn't reproduce the timing: the guard refuses creating a store.db directly, and 8x150 parallel `focus` runs against a first scan never hit the window. Store::open creates store.db with create_new, then migrates in a separate transaction. If the process dies in between, the file stays at user_version 0. open_existing (map, focus, share, import, person, watch, serve) then runs migration 1 with init=None, which returns StoreError::Io('a new store needs its workspace record'), mapped to `internal`. Tail::seq on such a file fails on 'no such table'.
findings.why: The pane draws an internal error instead of the not-a-workspace state that DR-57 requires ('never a blank'), until someone runs scan.
findings.fix: In open_existing, treat user_version 0 with no tables as 'no store' (return Ok(None)), so readers show the scan empty state. Or create the file under a temporary name and rename it into place after migration 1 commits.

verdicts.reason: I reproduced it myself on a fresh fixture with its own PLANROOM_DATA. I prepended '# local note' to platform/docker-compose.yml and scanned: 'Mapped 5 repos, 5 of them moved: 0 containers, 125 nodes'. `map` then shows only the 5 repo nodes. I restored the file (git status clean) and rescanned: 'Mapped 5 repos, 0 of them moved: 0 containers, 135 nodes, 17 hints', but `map` still shows 5 nodes. A fresh store over the same clean heads gives 10 nodes, including ws:container:grafana, orders-db, otel-collector, prometheus and redis. So the scan line and the map disagree, and two stores at the same heads give different maps. Code: the facts come from the working-tree walk (scan.rs:108). put_snapshot is ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING keyed by (repo, commit, purpose, packs_hash) (commit.rs:301-303). insert_facts runs only when `created` (commit.rs:156-157), and previous==snapshot reports Unchanged (commit.rs:160). The architecture's own rules conflict here: 'Deterministic. The same commit gives byte-identical facts' and 'The map holds only committed lines' (architecture.md:604, 609). The known-gaps table (architecture.md:1560-1572) doesn't list it. The map stays wrong with no recovery until HEAD moves, on the everyday first scan of a dirty repo. I keep it material.

I reproduced it myself on a fresh fixture and store. I made kit/scratch/deep/notes.txt and an empty kit/EMPTY_UNTRACKED; git status shows both as ??. After `scan`, `map --level code` lists kit:file:EMPTY_UNTRACKED and `map --level component` lists kit:dir:scratch/deep and kit:dir:scratch. Code: the directory set comes from every walked file, before verification (files.rs:96-100). An empty file and every directory get tree_evidence(), a Ref holding only the commit and branch (files.rs:66-71, 111, 141). Verifier::check for a Ref checks only that the commit and the ref exist (verify.rs:113-125). DR-81 deliberately gives directories a commit Ref, but the outcome is that untracked paths reach the map, against architecture.md:609. Minor is right.

I reproduced it myself. After a scan, `mv kit` out of the workspace and `scan`: 'Mapped 4 repos, 0 of them moved', yet `map` still lists kit:repo:kit. I then moved it back as kit2 and scanned: the map lists both kit:repo:kit and kit2:repo:kit2. Code: active_snapshots takes MAX(seq) per target over scan events, with no retirement (read.rs:113-129). commit_scan only adds or moves repos (commit.rs:146-170). No doc handles a repo that leaves the workspace; DR-74 routes a renamed repo directory through rescan.retarget, which is M1. I downgrade it to minor. The ghost repo is wrong, but it fails no tier A or B scenario on the fixture. It loses no data today. The 'only recovery deletes person events' harm needs M1 writes, and the planned event backups and restore (DR-53) also cover that case.

I reproduced it myself. I wrote a workspaces.json with top-level min_reader_version and future_key, and an entry carrying 'label', then ran `serve --detach --port 41777`. The rewritten file keeps only format and workspaces[{root, workspace_id, port}]; all three unknown fields are gone. Code: Workspaces and WorkspaceEntry have no #[serde(flatten)] extra (data.rs:49-61). record() reads, modifies and renames with no lock (data.rs:78-86), and bind() calls it (server/mod.rs:150-155). This contradicts contracts.md:14 ('Unknown fields are kept through #[serde(flatten)] extra and written back unchanged'), contracts.md:357 (the file is shared by every engine version and changes only by additions), and the AGENTS.md compatibility invariant. Once this build ships, its behaviour can't be fixed retroactively: it will erase a newer engine's fields, min_reader_version included, which defeats DR-78's guard. The lost-update race can also move a workspace's port. I keep it material, as a violation of the versioned-contract constraint and a cross-version data-loss risk.

I reproduced it myself with a fresh data root and two concurrent `serve --detach --json` runs in one workspace. Both returned ok:true, one with port 42129 pid 19455 and one with port 41155 pid 19456, and ps showed both processes alive. workspaces.json and serve.json recorded only 41155. I then killed both pids. Code: bind() reads workspaces.json, binds port 0 when no port is recorded, and records, all without a lock (server/mod.rs:126-158). announce() writes serve.json last-writer-wins. Minor is right: it needs a race on first use.

Confirmed by reading code. map::run calls top(), which runs active_set() (active_snapshots, then a separate SELECT for the last scan's link, read.rs:73-85) and facts(), then reads store.seq() afterwards (map.rs:31-40). Each runs as its own autocommit statement on the connection, with no surrounding read transaction. A commit between them yields content from N-1 under seq N, or a torn repo/link set. It stays minor because writes aren't built yet and the harm is latent.

Confirmed by reading code. start() awaits load(), then subscribes (store.ts:206-215). The first stream fetch sends no Last-Event-ID (lastId=null) and no since (local.ts:186-200). On the server, backlog() with since=None sets the cursor to tail.seq() (live.rs:43-46, routes.rs:359-370), and broadcast frames with seq <= cursor are filtered out. A commit after the map read and before the stream request therefore sends no frame. The first frame is a Ping, which the canvas ignores, and the canvas has no periodic refetch (store.ts:169-182). Minor.

Confirmed by reading code. In the non-detached path, cli::finish prints the announce envelope (server/mod.rs:52-56). On Err, serve(prepared) calls cli::finish::<()>(json, "serve", Err(e), ...) again (mod.rs:58-61), printing a second document. serve() can fail after the announce: the runtime build, or Store::open_existing returning None or Err (mod.rs:205-209). This breaks the AGENTS.md one-document rule only in a rare failure path, so it stays minor.

Confirmed by reading code. packs_hash() includes CARGO_PKG_VERSION (scan.rs:32-34). scan stores it through meta_insert_once (scan.rs:52-53), which is INSERT OR IGNORE (store lib.rs:147-153). After an engine upgrade, meta.packs_hash therefore keeps the first engine's hash while new snapshots carry the new one. No code reads it yet, so it stays minor and latent.

Confirmed by reading code. (a) share writes the bundle to disk, then meta_swaps share_snapshot_seq to the snapshot's seq (share.rs:73-82), regardless of any publish. (b) import reads seq (import.rs:173), then live_head pages events_after in a loop with no upper bound (import.rs:299-306), so head.changes can hold events past head.seq. The page uses head.seq as its row base (artifact.ts:229). Also, `after` starts at max(snapshot_seq, seq-HEAD_CHANGES), which silently drops older changes. Writes aren't applied yet, so it stays minor.

Confirmed by reading code. The start_live thread runs live.run once. On any Err it prints to stderr and exits the process only for SchemaMismatch (routes.rs:96-107). Live::run propagates every StoreError from data_version, check_version and drain through ? (live.rs:84-95). No SSE KeepAlive is configured (grep for keep_alive/KeepAlive in server/ finds nothing), so clients get neither events nor pings afterwards. Transient errors on a WAL read connection are uncommon, so it stays minor.

Confirmed by code and by a simulated state. Store::open creates the file with create_new, then migrates in a separate transaction (store lib.rs:59-70). open_existing migrates with init=None, and migration 1 then fails with 'a new store needs its workspace record' (lib.rs:121-124). I put an empty 0600 .planroom/store.db in a fresh fixture workspace. `focus --json` and `map --json` both return ok:false with code internal and the message 'Planroom hit a bug: a new store needs its workspace record'; before the file existed, focus returned the never-scanned empty state. The same path is reachable when a reader takes the migration lock first during a concurrent first scan. Minor.
